nodes.summary: Real-valued form of `LinearMap.IsSymmetric.apply_eigenvectorBasis`: the eigenvalue is a plain real scalar, with no `ℝ → 𝕜` coercion.
nodes.title: Eigenvector basis equation with real eigenvalues

nodes.summary: Bhatia–Davis inequality for a symmetric operator: the variance of `T` at a unit vector is at most `(M - μ) * (μ - m)`, where `μ` is the Rayleigh quotient.
nodes.title: Bhatia–Davis inequality

nodes.summary: The eigenvalues of a symmetric operator lie in `[m, M]` whenever its Rayleigh quotients do.
nodes.title: Eigenvalues lie within the Rayleigh quotient bounds

nodes.summary: The quadratic form of a two-sided inverse is the weighted average of the reciprocal eigenvalues.
nodes.title: Inverse quadratic form as a weighted average of reciprocal eigenvalues

nodes.summary: Kantorovich's inequality for a symmetric operator: for a unit vector `x`, the product of the Rayleigh quotient of `T` and the Rayleigh quotient of its two-sided inverse `S` is at most `(M + m)² / (4 * m * M)`.
nodes.title: Kantorovich's inequality

nodes.summary: Popoviciu's inequality for a symmetric operator: the variance of `T` at a unit vector is at most `((M - m) / 2)²`.
nodes.title: Popoviciu's inequality

nodes.summary: The Rayleigh quotient is the weighted average of the eigenvalues, with weights `((eigenvectorBasis).repr x i)²`.
nodes.title: Rayleigh quotient as a weighted average of eigenvalues

nodes.summary: The second-moment quadratic form is the weighted average of the squared eigenvalues.
nodes.title: Second moment as a weighted average of squared eigenvalues
Eigenbasis weights sum to the squared norm

nodes.summary: The variance of `T` at a unit vector is the weighted squared deviation of the eigenvalues from the Rayleigh quotient.
nodes.title: Operator variance as weighted squared deviation of eigenvalues

nodes.summary: Bhatia–Davis inequality, scalar weighted form: if the weights are nonnegative, sum to `1`, and every `λ i` lies in `[m, M]`, then the weighted variance is at most `(M - μ) * (μ - m)`, where `μ` is the weighted mean.
nodes.title: Bhatia–Davis inequality

nodes.summary: Kantorovich's inequality, scalar weighted form: if the weights are nonnegative, sum to `1`, every `λ i` lies in `[m, M]`, and `0 < m`, then `(∑ w i * λ i) * (∑ w i / λ i) ≤ (M + m)² / (4 * m * M)`.
nodes.title: Kantorovich's inequality

nodes.summary: Popoviciu's inequality, scalar weighted form: the weighted variance is at most `((M - m) / 2)²`.
nodes.title: Popoviciu's inequality

nodes.summary: The weighted variance equals the weighted squared deviation from the weighted mean.
nodes.title: Weighted variance as weighted squared deviation from the mean

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
